terms.gloss: Classmate with nickname 'Griz' (Grizzly)

proposed.ja: 「トーテム」……「インターネットのトーテムになりたい」

terms.gloss: Nickname of a stairway landing in the SPbU Philology building
terms.why_hard: Invented student nickname ('captain's bridge/bridge wing'), not a real landmark; keep the quotes and don't over-localize

terms.gloss: Nickname of a corridor in the philology faculty building

terms.gloss: Philology faculty and Oriental studies faculty of SPbU
terms.why_hard: Abbreviations recur constantly; must match fixed full forms throughout the book

proposed.en: the Philology faculty / the Oriental Studies faculty
proposed.ja: 文学部（言語学）／東洋学部

proposed.zh: “奥林波斯”学生美学与设计大赛

proposed.ja: デウス・エクス・マキナ（調停者）

terms.why_hard: Translating as rigid constitutional law rather than manipulative political maneuvering between rival factions.

proposed.ja: 牽制と均衡（チェック・アンド・バランス）

terms.gloss: Supreme Moderator (Durov's self-fashioned forum title)

terms.why_hard: Declined Russian film title; requires matching official franchise titles.

terms.why_hard: Cyrillic transliteration of an established film character.

terms.gloss: The Oracle from The Matrix (Russian dub uses Pythia)
terms.why_hard: Translating literally as 'Pythia' in English/Japanese rather than using the film's official localized name 'The Oracle'.

terms.gloss: to write code / program
terms.why_hard: Russian tech slang of the 2000s; overly formalizing loses the hacker subculture register.

terms.why_hard: Must accurately reflect the standard dubbed movie catchphrases in target languages.

proposed.ja: 「起きろ、ネオ。お前が救世主だ」

terms.gloss: Keanu Reeves, lead actor in The Matrix
terms.why_hard: Standard spelling across target cultures.

terms.gloss: Totem, Pavel Durov's early internet/hacker handle
terms.why_hard: Mistaking it for a common noun instead of Durov's famous online handle.

terms.gloss: ostentation, grandiosity, theatrical gravitas (Russian 2000s nuance)

terms.gloss: Benito Mussolini, Italian fascist dictator

terms.gloss: Martin Luther King Jr.
terms.why_hard: Standard historical name; ensure standard localized honorific/suffix conventions.

terms.gloss: to stress out, fret, or sweat the small stuff
terms.why_hard: Colloquial verb that shouldn't be translated literally as taking a steam bath.

terms.gloss: the university-wide portal and forum created by Durov for SPbGU students

terms.gloss: Colloquial shortening of 'экономический факультет' — the economics faculty of St Petersburg State University.
terms.why_hard: Casual clipping must be preserved in register, not expanded to full official name.

proposed.ja: トラフィック——生身の人間のトラフィック

terms.gloss: Philology faculty of SPbGU, Durov's own faculty; recurring location ('дворик филфака').

terms.gloss: The building's doorwoman/watch guard controlling access with a propusk system.
terms.why_hard: Culture-specific Soviet-era figure; 'caretaker' or 'porter' misses the gatekeeping connotation, and the gender is unspecified.

terms.gloss: Allusion to an earlier scene in the Idiot bar (Dostoevsky-themed St Petersburg hangout) involving Americans; Durov mentally 'sends greetings' to them while smiling at the doorkeeper.
terms.why_hard: Backward reference to a prior segment; translator must know who these Americans are or the line reads as nonsense.

proposed.en: the Americans from the Idiot bar
proposed.ja: バー「イディオット」のアメリカ人たち

proposed.ja: 微笑み、微笑み、また微笑み

terms.gloss: The small patch of hallway where the hip crowd habitually hangs out.

terms.gloss: Recruitment metaphor — 'recruiting supporters' as if running an intelligence operation; recurring spy framing of Durov's flyering.

terms.gloss: Campus slang for officials/staff who tear down posters.

proposed.ja: ポスター剥がしの連中

proposed.ja: 大学側は掲示板には勝てない

proposed.zh: 挎着手拿包的拜金靓妹
proposed.ja: クラッチバッグの“グラマー系”女子

terms.gloss: How to snag a rich guy (хомут = halter/noose; 'lasso a moneybags').

proposed.zh: 把那男生说得一文不值
proposed.ja: 男をこてんぱんにこき下ろしていた

proposed.ja: 学部長は彫刻を収集している

terms.why_hard: Chain of three escalating stunts; 'Харлей' is a brand, камзол an 18th-century garment — register and era of each item must survive.

proposed.ja: まさにデウス・エクス・マキナ

terms.gloss: Literally 'the chosen one' — mock-solemn label for the student Durov has picked.

terms.why_hard: The phrase invokes the Russian archetype of the sympathetic, cultivated idler rather than merely describing a sensitive soul.

proposed.zh: 奥勃洛莫夫那颗温柔的心
proposed.ja: オブローモフの繊細な魂

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, the future founder of VKontakte and the central subject of the biography.
terms.why_hard: His surname must be transliterated consistently and should not be localized or translated semantically.

terms.gloss: A comic aside noting that Durov and Goncharov both bear surnames formed from ordinary Russian words.
terms.why_hard: It imitates an elevated exclamation while joking about aristocratic-looking Russian surnames, a wordplay easily lost in translation.

proposed.ja: おお、ロシア貴族の姓よ！

terms.gloss: Durov’s literature teacher, who encourages argumentative classroom discussion.
terms.why_hard: The surname requires one consistent transliteration across the book.

terms.gloss: The opening of the proverb meaning that work will not run away and therefore need not be hurried.
terms.why_hard: A literal rendering about a wolf is opaque unless the procrastination-friendly force of the full proverb is conveyed.

terms.gloss: To hold forth in a didactic, self-important, lecturing manner.
terms.why_hard: It is mildly mocking and more colloquial than the neutral verb “to lecture.”

proposed.zh: 继续摆出导师口吻说教
proposed.ja: なおも教訓めいた口調で論じた

terms.gloss: Ivan Goncharov, the nineteenth-century Russian novelist who wrote Oblomov.
terms.why_hard: Readers without Russian literary context may not recognize either the author or the argument about his cultural influence.

terms.gloss: A socially approved stance of active, purposeful engagement, expressed in a stock Soviet-era formula.
terms.why_hard: Literal “active life position” sounds unnatural in English but the phrase’s ideological, formulaic flavor matters.

terms.gloss: Andrei Stolz, Oblomov’s energetic, rational foil, characterized here as mechanical and emotionally limited.
terms.why_hard: “Mechanistic” refers to the character’s programmatic efficiency, not literally to machinery.

terms.gloss: An ironic reference to Russia as “our wonderful/peculiar country.”
terms.why_hard: The adjective can mean lovely or strange, and the sentence relies on that sardonic ambiguity.

proposed.en: this strange and wonderful country of ours
proposed.zh: 我们这个奇妙而古怪的国家
proposed.ja: この何とも奇妙なわが国

terms.gloss: A person or stock dramatic figure who habitually voices reasoned judgments and moral arguments.
terms.why_hard: It does not simply mean a reasonable person; in Russian it often suggests a compulsive, somewhat tiresome arguer.

proposed.zh: 这个爱讲道理的辩论家

terms.gloss: Colloquial phrasing for aggressively taking a line opposed to everyone else.
terms.why_hard: A literal translation involving driving or chasing would miss the youthful slang and confrontational tone.

proposed.ja: 皆に逆らってまくし立てる

terms.gloss: Fyodor Dostoevsky, the canonical nineteenth-century Russian novelist whom Durov also attacked in class.
terms.why_hard: The established spelling or transcription differs by target language and must remain consistent.

terms.gloss: The Cherry Orchard, Anton Chekhov’s play about an indebted landowning family losing its estate.

terms.gloss: Children formed by the Russian intelligentsia’s educated, cultivated, morally self-conscious values.
terms.why_hard: Russian intelligenty denotes a cultural and ethical social identity, not merely intelligent children.

proposed.zh: 出身知识分子家庭的孩子们
proposed.ja: インテリ家庭の子供たち

terms.gloss: The merchant class personified by Lopakhin, the self-made businessman in The Cherry Orchard.

proposed.en: the merchant class, embodied by Lopakhin
proposed.zh: 以洛巴辛为代表的商人阶层
proposed.ja: ロパーヒンに体現された商人階級

terms.gloss: A class-charged image of coarse commercial forces trampling upon Ranevskaya’s delicate aristocratic sensibility.
terms.why_hard: The boots-versus-lace contrast must preserve both social caricature and the narrator’s irony.

proposed.en: stomping in its boots over Ranevskaya’s lacework soul
proposed.zh: 穿着靴子闯进拉涅夫斯卡娅那颗蕾丝般纤细的心

terms.gloss: Durov’s description of Lopakhin as a practical man who acts rather than merely talks or feels.
terms.why_hard: “Man of action” carries the intended approving contrast with the passive landowners better than literal “man of business.”

proposed.en: Lopakhin is a man of action
proposed.ja: ロパーヒンは行動の人だ

terms.gloss: The landowning estate class of imperial Russia, typically owners of rural estates and formerly of serfs.
terms.why_hard: Generic “landlords” loses the specific historical class identity and its revolutionary-era connotations.

terms.gloss: A hostile label for the Bolshevik or Soviet authorities who confiscated the family ancestors’ property, portraying them as parasitic Reds.
terms.why_hard: It fuses anti-Communist “Reds” with the insult “dependents/freeloaders,” not a formal political designation.

terms.gloss: A contemptuous image of undeserving low people receiving everything through revolutionary redistribution.
terms.why_hard: The dehumanizing class resentment is deliberate; smoothing it into “the undeserving” would weaken the passage.

proposed.zh: 那些不劳而获、占尽一切的渣滓
proposed.ja: すべてをせしめる卑賤な連中

terms.gloss: By every available means, whether fair or underhanded.
terms.why_hard: A word-for-word rendering about truths and untruths would not communicate the idiom.

terms.gloss: Mednikov’s affectionate school nickname, “Griz,” shortened from grizzly bear and linked to his surname’s bear root.
terms.why_hard: The nickname depends on Russian wordplay between Mednikov, medved meaning bear, and “grizzly.”

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov's student site hosting lecture notes and essays for the philology faculty

terms.gloss: Student-written summaries of lectures; course notes/essays in the Russian university sense

proposed.en: notes and study write-ups from lectures
proposed.ja: 講義ノート・レポート

terms.gloss: Mid-course oral assessment/seminar exam in Russian universities
terms.why_hard: Not a 'colloquium' in the English conference sense; it is a graded oral checkpoint

proposed.ja: 中間口頭試問（コロキウム）

terms.gloss: Classical philology — the father's professorship at St Petersburg State University's philology faculty
terms.why_hard: Needs to stay consistent with other segments' rendering of филфак and the father's chair

terms.gloss: Students' nickname ('Durov's corner') for the nook by the department, honoring the professor — a pun anticipating the son's site
terms.why_hard: The pun linking father, corner, and later site must survive; a literal translation kills the joke

terms.gloss: Ageism — here Durov's bias in favor of the young, against older authority
terms.why_hard: English 'ageism' usually means bias against the old as discrimination; here it is a personal creed of youth-worship

proposed.zh: 年龄歧视（崇年轻、贬年长）

terms.gloss: Recurring ironic epithet for Durov as an idol/icon of his admirers ('fame didn't go to the totem's head')
terms.why_hard: Must match the totem metaphor used across the book; replacing with 'star' breaks the motif

terms.gloss: English-in-Russian term for Wikipedia-style collective work, foreshadowing VKontakte
terms.why_hard: Keep it marked as borrowed English or normalize it; decide once for all Anglophone borrowings in the book

proposed.ja: マス・コラボレーション（大規模協働）

terms.term: не только славу, но и хлеб
terms.gloss: 'Not only fame but bread' — i.e., a livelihood, money
terms.why_hard: Literal 'bread' sounds odd in English/Chinese; needs the livelihood sense while staying light

proposed.en: not just fame but a living
proposed.zh: 不仅带来名声，还能糊口
proposed.ja: 名声だけでなく糊口の資にもなる

terms.gloss: Gazprom, the Russian state gas giant, shorthand for a rich corporate employer

proposed.zh: 俄罗斯天然气工业股份公司（Gazprom）

terms.gloss: 'Hydrocarbon outfit' — dismissive slang for an oil-and-gas company
terms.why_hard: Контора is derogatory ('outfit/shoppy'); 'company' loses the sneer

terms.gloss: Anna Dmitrievna Bertova, an old acquaintance/teacher figure addressed formally by Durov
